videos.role: Monthly-to-weekly higher-timeframe framework
deep_read_findings: This is the highest layer of the four-part top-down framework.

videos.title: ICT Mentorship Core Content - Month 12 - Short Term Top Down Analysis
videos.role: Daily-to-four-hour short-term framework
deep_read_findings: The daily chart is treated as subordinate to the monthly/weekly conclusions and as the main short-term directional filter.

The four-hour chart is used to refine active ranges, PD arrays, liquidity and potential entries, but should remain aligned with the daily narrative.
The lesson strongly supports the curriculum rule that lower-timeframe bullish/bearish patterns are not meaningful without higher-timeframe context.

videos.title: ICT Mentorship Core Content - Month 12 - Intraday Top Down Analysis

videos.title: Ends Series Vol 1
videos.role: Problem-definition and mindset transition from studying ICT to applying a trading model to real-life financial constraints.
concepts: trading as a potential income stream
transition from student mindset to operator mindset
findings: ICT introduces the four-part series as a practical transition from the 2022 mentorship model into real-life application.
The first part focuses on identifying the financial 'ends' that create pressure and can distort trading decisions.
He emphasizes budgeting, distinguishing essential expenses from excess/lifestyle spending, and avoiding the social-media wealth image.
This is explicitly not a new technical trading model; it is mindset and life-structure material that sits around the trading process.
videos.curriculum_role: Professional practice / trading-life management lab, not a technical prerequisite.

videos.title: Ends Series Vol 2
videos.role: Solution and financial-structure lesson: keep stable income while developing trading and other income streams.
findings: ICT frames the 'solution' as developing additional income rather than immediately replacing employment.
He explicitly warns against assuming that early trading success means readiness to leave a job and describes initial luck as potentially misleading.
The lesson separates employment, investment and business income as different branches of a broader financial plan.

For the curriculum, the durable trading lesson is delayed gratification and avoiding financial pressure on a developing trading account; the U.S.-specific tax/legal discussion is not portable to other jurisdictions.
videos.curriculum_role: Professional practice / financial-risk-management lab.

videos.title: Ends Series Vol 3
videos.role: Plan-definition lesson turning the financial goal into a constrained, low-frequency trading process.
findings: ICT frames the series as a practical application of the 2022 mentorship model rather than a new model.
The case study uses one E-mini S&P contract, a fixed four-point stop and a five-and-a-quarter-point objective, with no pyramiding or partials.
The process is restricted to AM/PM index-futures windows and uses medium/high-impact news days to narrow the weekly focus.
For bullish weekly expansion, the model waits for sell-side liquidity to be taken, displacement higher, then a fair-value-gap entry; bearish logic is the mirror image.
The lesson explicitly says not to chase price after a missed FVG fill and to allow trades to pass when the required risk parameters are unavailable.
videos.curriculum_role: Applied execution-protocol lab built on the 2022 mentorship model.

videos.title: Ends Series Vol 4
videos.role: Process/rules lesson: operationalizes the constrained E-mini model and adds failure, re-entry and missed-entry protocols.
findings: The lesson turns the prior plan into explicit operational rules: one E-mini, fixed four-point stop, 5.25-point target, no partials and constrained session windows.
For a bullish weekly expansion, the examples repeatedly use a raid below previous week/day/session lows, displacement higher and an FVG entry; bearish logic reverses the conditions.
Lower timeframes are used only to refine an FVG when the resulting stop remains within the fixed risk constraint.
If no FVG permits the required stop, ICT says to do nothing rather than force a higher-risk trade.
The transcript includes a defined re-entry protocol after a stop and a rule to stop trading for the week after another loss, emphasizing low frequency and acceptance of missed moves.
For larger FVGs, consequent encroachment is introduced as the entry reference to preserve the fixed stop constraint.
videos.curriculum_role: Applied execution/risk protocol lab; one of the strongest practical bridges from ICT 2022 model theory to a repeatable routine.

videos.title: ICT Institutional Price Action - Micro-Market Structure & Time & Price Concepts Part 02
videos.role: Micro-market structure, time/price and session-conditioned order-block execution
deep_read_findings: The lesson begins with higher-timeframe direction before dropping to a five-minute chart, explicitly tying low-timeframe analysis to the larger premise.
ICT uses a defined intraday window, bearish displacement, a lower-timeframe up-close candle/order block and a prior low as the prospective sell-side liquidity objective.
The sequence is therefore conditional: higher-timeframe bias → session/time window → displacement → retracement/entry reference → liquidity objective.
The lesson emphasizes that an entry does not have to occur at the higher-timeframe order block itself; lower-timeframe confirmation can refine the risk.
After the stated liquidity objective is reached, ICT reassesses rather than mechanically maintaining the original directional bias.
ICT also describes a time stop for an unproductive London setup, reinforcing that both time and price are part of the framework.
The session windows and price levels in the recording are historical examples; they should be taught as ICT's model and tested on the relevant instrument rather than assumed to guarantee outcomes.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 1
videos.role: Foundational trading-plan architecture and key support/resistance
findings: ICT frames the plan as a multi-stage process: anticipation, execution, management and reactionary decision-making.
The anticipatory stage is centered on weekly and daily analysis rather than constantly hunting lower-timeframe entries.

Key support/resistance is treated as a prerequisite for entries and exits; the transcript says levels should be identified from the 60-minute chart up to the monthly chart, with daily analysis emphasized.
Macro/intermarket inputs such as rates, COT, indices, seasonality and correlated markets are used before execution.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 2
videos.role: Market-profile classification and condition-dependent tool selection
findings: The lesson emphasizes defining the market profile before choosing the analytical tools.
Trend-oriented analysis is presented as less appropriate when the prevailing profile is reversal-oriented.
The student is encouraged to define in advance what evidence would invalidate the profile rather than changing the narrative after price moves.
This directly supports the curriculum rule that ICT tools are conditional on the diagnosed market environment.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 3
videos.role: COT / positioning context
findings: The archive describes this lesson as teaching the power of the Commitment of Traders report and how ICT uses it to track what he calls 'Smart Money.'
The durable curriculum role is positioning/context analysis rather than an entry trigger.
COT should therefore be taught as a slow-moving contextual input that can support or challenge a market thesis, not as a standalone buy/sell signal.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 4
videos.role: Timeframe-tool architecture and chart-template workflow
findings: ICT assigns different analytical jobs to different timeframes instead of treating every timeframe as interchangeable.
The hierarchy carries higher-timeframe support/resistance downward while lower charts add progressively finer structure and timing.
The transcript places monthly pivots on 4H, weekly pivots on 1H, and daily pivots on 15M/5M in this framework.
The five-minute chart is treated as execution-oriented while retaining the higher-timeframe premise.
This is a direct source for the university's eventual timeframe-roles course.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 5
videos.role: Intermediate-term planning and intermarket thesis construction
findings: ICT builds an intermediate-term currency thesis from a daily chart and a broad intermarket checklist before moving to lower timeframes.
The framework includes yields, Treasury futures, DXY, positioning/open interest and major risk assets.
Lower timeframes are used for execution after the intermediate thesis and significant support/resistance are established.
The lesson separates anticipation from execution and is therefore useful for teaching students not to let a five-minute pattern create a trade without a larger thesis.
Historical percentage and pip targets are recorded as examples from the lesson, not as independently validated expectations.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 6
videos.role: Short-term market-structure planning
findings: ICT defines a short-term trade as intraday through roughly five days in the framework and prioritizes higher-timeframe structure over temporary lower-timeframe flow.
Nested swing points are used to distinguish short-, intermediate- and long-term structure.
The framework uses higher-timeframe support/resistance and then applies lower-timeframe tools for the actual trade.
This is a key prerequisite for the later market-structure curriculum because it shows that structure has multiple degrees of swing.

videos.title: ICT – Trading Plan Development 7
videos.role: Intraday London-session plan and conditional participation rules
findings: ICT's intraday plan starts with weekly/daily directional context and then uses the Asian range and London timing as the execution environment.
The initial move outside the Asian range is evaluated as a possible stop raid/false breakout rather than automatically chased.
ICT assigns daily/4H charts to directional context, 1H to weekly swings and support/resistance, and 15M to intraday management.
He identifies conditions for standing aside, including major rate announcements, holidays, unexpected events, already-reached weekly objectives and an unusually wide Asian range.
This is a strong example of the user's desired 'what market conditions must exist before I use this concept?' structure.
